C0.quote: designing voting rules that take as input the ordinal preferences of n agents
C0.note: Voting rule design with distortion guarantees.

C1.quote: simultaneously achieve near-optimal distortion guarantees in both distortion worlds
C1.note: Distortion bounds (upper and lower) for rules; AL is only weakly applicable (rule design), but WD is dominant. Lower bounds are also distortion results.

C2.1.quote: Collectively, they form a preference profile

C2.2.quote: L(A) to denote the set of all rankings (linear orders)

C2.3.quote: each agent i ∈ N has a utility function ui : A → R⩾0
C2.3.note: Cardinal preferences/utilities and metric distances are held attitudes.

C2.4.quote: We assume that the preference profile stems from underlying cardinal preferences
C2.4.note: The ranking is described as the agent's preference and tied to cardinal preferences via consistency; there is no statement about submission versus truthful reporting. The intro mentions 'report', but the model has no separate notation.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: The consistency relation is defined for both metric and utility frameworks.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: the quality of each alternative is determined based on the sum
C5.1.note: Distortion, social welfare and social cost are the criteria.

C5.2.quote: worst-case distortion of f (~σ ) on any utility profile ~u ⊲U ~σ
C5.2.note: Distortion is evaluated against cardinal utilities/metric costs defined separately from the rankings.

VOT.note: Agents are only the source of the input; they take no action in the model.

DES.note: The designer is mentioned in the introduction, but their choice or objective is not modelled formally.
